statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail lifts from 5 to 8 as Globex reopens and a price path exists again, but the reopen is tight and two-sided and absorbed the late Kharg Island headlines without a gap, while stress holds at 73 on WTI at a three-month $94.33, Brent near $99 and a 10-year at 4.806%.
recommendation: Conditions remain consistent with normal mean-reverting behaviour. The Nasdaq-100 closed 107 points above its session low after a two-sided fade, index internals were dispersed rather than uniformly directional, and the 22:00 UTC Globex reopen produced no gap and no directional leg. Cross-asset channels are firm but conflicting, which raises stress rather than tail. The narrow flagged window covers the Tokyo cash open, the horizon's first genuine liquidity discontinuity and the first session able to price both the yen at its strongest since February and the reported explosions near Kharg Island. Tail remains far below the block threshold across all 24 forecast hours.
headline: NQ reopens on Globex near 29,525 with no gap after NDX closed at 29,507.70, down 0.12%; WTI at a three-month $94.33 and a yen at 152.89 keep stress at 73 while a tight two-sided reopen holds tail at 8
body:
Nasdaq-100 futures reopened on Globex at 22:00 UTC after the daily CME maintenance halt and trade near 29,525, down about 0.05%, inside a roughly 36-point band of 29,503.00 to 29,539.25 on very thin volume in the first minutes of the new session. That reopen is the single most useful observation available right now: it absorbed the late-Tuesday reports of explosions near Kharg Island without a gap and without a directional leg. A price path exists again after an hour in which none could form, and the path that exists is tight and two-sided. That is the direct opposite of the structure capable of overwhelming a mean-reversion basket, which is why tail lifts only from 5 to 8 as trading resumes.

The verified cash session behind that reopen was orderly. The Nasdaq-100 closed at 29,507.70, down 36.45 points or 0.12%, inside a 29,400.70 to 29,655.73 range and 107 points above the session low. The Dow closed 1.18% lower and the S&P 500 0.58% lower, so the Nasdaq was the least weak of the three, and index internals were unusually dispersed rather than uniformly directional: Intel gained about 9% on a processor pricing plan and Corning about 7.6% on a Verizon optical fibre agreement, while Amgen fell about 10% and Novartis about 14% after a failed heart disease trial. Qualcomm signed an AI chip agreement with Amazon valued at up to $60 billion. Dispersion of that kind is the signature of rotation, not of a single one-way index leg, and it is the reason the dominant mode stays mixed.

Stress is a separate matter and stays high at 73. WTI settled at $94.33, up 1.69% and a three-month high on a sixth consecutive advance, with Brent at $99.39. The drivers are verified and unresolved: US strikes on Iranian tankers linked to the Revolutionary Guard, Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure that halted operations and injured 73 people, and the late reports of explosions near Kharg Island, Iran's principal export terminal. Strait of Hormuz transit has been running near ten commodity ships a day. Alongside energy, the yen reached 152.89 per dollar, its strongest since February, with market-implied odds of a Bank of Japan hike to 1.25% at 97% for the September 18 meeting; cross-border yen borrowing stood at a record 360 trillion yen in March, so a disorderly carry unwind is a credible transmission channel. The 10-year Treasury yield closed at 4.806%, up 2.2 basis points and near the top of its range, while the VIX at 15.72 remains unremarkable.

Those channels are firm and conflicting, which raises stress rather than tail. Confidence holds at 88 on a complete and current evidence base spanning verified index and futures levels, volatility, yields, both crude benchmarks, the currency channel and the seven-day calendar; the only limitation is the thin overnight book, which restricts how much the reopen path can be relied on. Mapped policy state: EA_ON, with tail far below the block threshold across all 24 forecast hours.

lookbackSummary: Across the last 24 hours the assessment stayed inside the EA_ON band without interruption. Tail ran between 6 and 10 from Monday evening through Tuesday morning, stepped up to 15 in the 14:00 UTC slot on an observed cash-open downside leg that left NQ near the session low, then fell back through 8, 7 and 6 as that leg was fully retraced, ran at 8 through the power hour and closed the window at 5 during the CME maintenance halt, when no price path could form at all. Stress rose steadily from 62 on Monday evening to 72 by Tuesday afternoon as crude extended on the Saudi facility strikes and the tanker exchanges, eased to the high 60s through the afternoon, and held at 72 into the close as WTI pressed to a three-month high. Confidence improved monotonically from 78 to 89 as overnight inference was replaced by live cash-session observation, easing to 88 in the final halt hour. The dominant mode was mixed for 22 of the 23 published hours because cross-asset signals kept diverging from Nasdaq price action, and turned to trend-down only for the single hour that carried the cash-open decline. The 09:00 UTC slot has no published assessment and is marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The horizon opens with Globex newly reopened, so conditional tail sits at 8 rather than the halt-hour floor. It steps to 10 at the 00:00 UTC Tokyo cash open, which is the flagged window and the horizon's first genuine liquidity discontinuity, because that is the first session able to price both the strongest yen since February and the late reports of explosions near Kharg Island. Conditional tail then settles between 7 and 9 through the Asian session, lifts to 9 at the 07:00 UTC European cash open, and holds in the 7 to 8 range through the European morning and the US pre-market. The horizon peak of 13 falls in the 14:00 UTC hour, the first full hour after Wednesday's US cash open, because opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks is the specific structure capable of overwhelming mean reversion; nothing about that structure is observed, and Tuesday's equivalent slot reached 15 before fully retracing within the hour. Scores then decay through midday before lifting to 11 at the 17:00 UTC pairing of Apple's confirmed product keynote with the US 10-year note auction, and the horizon closes at 5 in the next CME maintenance halt. All 24 slots stay inside the EA_ON band. Three unresolved channels could force a step change in either direction: Middle East energy, where Kharg Island is now involved and Hormuz transit is heavily constrained; the yen carry unwind ahead of the September 18 Bank of Japan meeting; and Thursday's PPI as the first of the week's two inflation prints.
